Hello all,

I am writing this to be informative, not to sway you, but to at least make you aware of the candidate you are voting for. I was a bystander during this election cycle until a call I had with my mom. We talked about college, my grades, how I’m doing, what’s new and, of course, politics came up. Once my mom heard that I was supporting Donald Trump I was immediately cut off. My mom expressed her disdain of Donald Trump and his treatment of women, and after she had cooled off she told me “I can’t hear your reasons for voting Trump because, honestly, he makes me sick”. I understand this feeling, I get it when I imagine Hillary in office but I am not afraid of discussing the reasoning or politics of it. I write this now because even though my mom can’t stand to hear my reasoning maybe she can read it and make up her mind after getting both sides. If this reaches you I want you to know I heard your side, I’d like it if you could hear mine.

I can’t say Donald is the most inspiring presidential candidate and he certainly isn’t the president every American dreams of, but he is the most important one during this campaign season. This election has been plagued with some of the worse election etiquette I’ve ever seen, and I hope for my future and ours, that it won’t always be such a shit show, that only proves to the American people that neither candidate is fit for Presidency.

Donald Trump has some serious faults, no one who has looked at him closely(or even through a pair of binoculars backwards) can deny that, but try doing the same to Hillary and you will be deflected. There have been incredibly damning pieces of information coming from Wikileaks(1), the FBI(wasn’t included because FBI.vault.gov was down at the time), and Project(2) Veritas(3). I haven’t read through all the emails that have caught my interest but the theme behind them is clear, “Hillary can’t be trusted.” Her associates from the Democratic National Committee have been caught in a whirlwind of fraud and legal trouble regarding biased polling and accepting money from foreign donors. Associates and friends of hers have been caught on tape admitting to voter fraud and “using mentally ill people” at campaigns. Voter fraud is a serious issue that needs to be dealt with, but they go on to admit to inciting the violence at Trump rallies, pushing his agenda towards one of bullying and intimidation. Trump does have a history of insulting people, and even races, but he has never used tactics that put another person’s life in danger which when it comes down to it “sticks and stones break my bones but words will never hurt me”. Trump may be president in which case he will have to step up his game in accepting the diversity that makes America great, but Hillary will be a president that tears America apart.

As I have been watching Wikileaks being torn down by the media they incriminate, in the new documents released in the latest “Podesta Dump”(4), I was wondering what other time has Wikileaks faced monumental backlash, not only from the government, but from large media sources as well. Wikileaks has a history of being involved in shady politics because it uses shady means to get their information but that information has never been false so far. The same media that is bashing Wikileaks for being on Russia’s side was referencing their documents and admiring the fortitude of Wikileaks to stand up to corrupt regimes around the world. John Podesta has not denied the authenticity of the emails(5) either and blaming the Russians for interference on Trumps behalf is too hypocritical. All the while Hillary has been caught with donations from so many foreign donors(6) during her time as Secretary of State(7) and on the campaign trail(8). It seems both nominees are getting help from groups that shouldn’t be involved in this fight yet neither are denying the assistance. The only thing that is scarier to me than a President owing favors to another country because of what was done during the campaign is that President being in control of the main sources of media. This is effectively eviscerating the First amendment(9). It is clear why the news sources like MSNBC, ABC, CBS, the New York Times, Politico and CNN(among many others)(10) have been so lacking in their duty to inform the public. The Podesta Emails show that Hillary Clintons staffers met with the heads of many news sources days before the official announcement (11) for candidacy. Being friendly with the press is a smart move for a politician but wining and dining them the night before you plan to become President is going to give them some sort of bias(even if unintended). Emails have proven Hillary’s “interviews” to be scripted beforehand(12), which creates a disingenuous candidate at best, and at worst a state propaganda machine operating as if it is without bias.

With facts showing that Hillary has worked with media in an almost state-controlled environment, the picture clearly shows Hillary is already working towards the removal of the freedom of press from the 1st amendment. I’m not willing to let any of the freedoms I was born with, and promised at birth, be taken away. Damn the “you can’t be entitled” bullshit, we are entitled to freedom of the press as well as the other guarantees of the Constitution and no one who works against those principles is going to work for America.

Yours Truly,

Your Son

There are two competing methodological approaches in software development today. The approach often idealized by corporate types is what I call the ‘million monkeys approach’. That’s the approach where each project takes 10 times more engineers to complete the same project, but allows those engineers to be mediocre (or moreso requires them to be as such lest they start pointing out too many obvious engineering problems). This results in code bases that are a horrific mess, a work environment that is totally politicized, legitimate engineering concerns that are ignored or punished for being raised, and an order of magnitude more cost. Once all the non-code-monkey level of talent jumps ship (and right soon), only through sheer throughput of human misery does the project get shipped — often months or years behind.
